sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Analyse any three characteristics of road transport in India.
questions.answer: (1) Roads provide door to door service by means of a rickshaw, car, bicycle, bus, scooter or a truck. It is through roads that we reach railway stations, airports and seaports. (2) It is the cheapest and the most convenient mode of transportation for a few people and relatively smaller amount of goods over shorter distances. (3) Roads connect rural areas to the urban areas and can be constructed in all types of terrains like hills, deserts, mountain and plateaus.

or.q: Analyse any three characteristics of rail transport in India.
or.answer: (1) This is the cheapest transport by which thousands of people can travel together from one corner of the country to another for the purpose of ducation, business, siteseeing, pilgrimage or visiting friends or relatives. One can have comfortable night journey as it has berths and washrooms in sleeper coaches. Railways are generally used for long distances. (2) It carries country’s largest amount of bulky goods like coal, cement, food grains, fertilizer, petroleum, automobiles etc. from mines to industries and from industries to the areas of consumption. (3) It is the largest network in Asia (over 64,000 km), the largest government undertaking, divided into 16 zones, with modern facilities like e-tickets and electric locomotives.

questions.q: Analyse any three aspects of village roads.
questions.answer: (1) These provide links from village to village and village to main road in the rural areas. (2) About 80% of the total road length in India is categorize as rural roads. (3) They help farmers take produce to markets, give access to schools and hospitals and support rural development; many are still kuchcha and get damaged in rain.

questions.q: How do roads contribute to the social and economic growth of a country? Explain three reasons.
questions.answer: (1) Roads play an important role in connecting people and also in ensuring socio-economic growth of a country as under: Roads connect rural areas to the urban areas and can be constructed in all types of terrains like hills, deserts, mountain and plateaus. (2) It is through roads that we reach railway stations, airports and seaports. (3) The government has launched a major road development project linking north, south, east and west India.This will reduce time and fuel.

questions.q: Why is there a dense rail network in the Gangetic plain but not in hilly and desert areas? Explain.
questions.answer: (1) The Gangetic plain is level, so railways are easy and cheap to build; hills and deserts make construction difficult and costly. (2) He alsotold that these areas are food bowl of India and most of the crops grown hereare taken to other parts of the country through railways. Regions which are densely populated and have more movements are definitelywell connected with railways. It is very useful for transporting heavy and bulky goods. (3) It has many large cities and industries, while deserts and hills have few people and little economic activity.

questions.q: 'From olden days till now waterways have been an important means of transportation.' Examine.
questions.answer: (1) It is the cheapest means as compared to other means of transport because it involves no expenditure on construction other than maintenance. Railways involve high construction and maintenance cost. (2) It carries country’s largest amount of bulky goods like coal, cement, food grains, fertilizer, petroleum, automobiles etc. from mines to industries and from industries to the areas of consumption. It is very useful for transporting heavy and bulky goods. A ship can carry lakhs of tonnes of goods at a time. (3) It is fuel-efficient and eco-friendly; inland waterways (NW-1, NW-2, NW-3) reduce traffic on roads and ocean routes carry most of India's foreign trade.

questions.q: Why are transport and communication called the lifelines of a country? Explain in six points.
questions.answer: (1) Transport facilitates trade and commerce by carrying goods from the areas of production to that of consumption. (2) Goods from the areas that have surplus are shifted to those areas which are deficient in those items. (3) Railways facilitate the movement of both freight and passengers and contribute to the growth of our economy. (4) Communication keeps us informed about the world’s events and trends. (5) (c) E-Commerce: Facility available for sale and purchase of goods through internet and fax. (6) Air transport is considering that world is becoming a global village.

questions.q: Explain the importance of air transport and of water transport for India.
questions.answer: (1) It is the fastest means of transport and one can reach the destination in a few hours covering the distance of hundreds of kilometers. (2) Water: The construction, repair and maintenance cost is less than other means of transport. It is the cheapest means as compared to other means of transport because it involves no expenditure on construction other than maintenance. (3) It is fuel efficient and environment friendly means of transportation.
